components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The optional honorific title of the pet owner (e.g. MR, MRS, MS, DR).
            When supplied it is prepended, after a single space, to the lastName to compose
            the owner's 'salutation'.
          type: string

## What I did

Converted owner deletion to a soft-delete and made the create endpoint's checks ignore deleted owners.

**Model** — `Owner.java`: added a `deleted` boolean field (`@Column(name = "deleted")`, defaults `false`) with `isDeleted()`/`setDeleted(...)`.

**Delete pipeline** — `DeleteOwner.java`: instead of `ownerRepository.delete(owner)`, it now sets `owner.setDeleted(true)` and `ownerRepository.save(owner)`. The `{ownerId}.DELETE.yml` pipeline (load → delete → respond with no content, all under `transaction`) is unchanged, so it still returns 2xx and the row is retained. `GET /api/owners/{id}` therefore keeps returning the owner, now with `deleted: true`.

**Create checks** — both now skip flagged owners:
- `EnsureUniqueIdentity.java`: `continue` on `existing.isDeleted()`, so a soft-deleted owner no longer triggers the 409 household-duplicate block.
- `AssignPossibleDuplicate.java`: same skip, so a deleted owner isn't treated as a soft match either.

**API contract** — `openapi.yml`: added a `deleted` boolean property to the `Owner` response schema (the DTO is generated from this spec; MapStruct auto-maps `Owner.isDeleted()` → `OwnerDto.deleted`).

**Schema** — added `deleted BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL` to the `owners` table in all four DB schemas (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres). The `DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL` guarantees the seed rows (which don't list the column) load as `false` into the primitive field.

## Notes
- Tests run under the `hsqldb, spring-data-jpa` profile with `ddl-auto=none`, so the hsqldb `schema.sql` is what's exercised.
- I left the legacy `JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl`/JPA impls untouched: they're not on the active profile and already omit the extended owner columns, so touching them would be inconsistent and out of scope.

Test results: `AcceptanceTest` (both `coreSoftDeleteFlagsAndRetains` and `coreDeletedOwnerIgnoredByDuplicateCheck`) and the full suite — **Tests run: 2, Failures: 0, Errors: 0**, BUILD SUCCESS.
